questions.prompt: What is the main goal of partitioning (sharding)?

options.text: To keep a full copy of all data on every node
To split the dataset so each node holds a subset, letting capacity grow with the cluster
To encrypt the data
To remove the need for replication

questions.explanation: Partitioning splits data across nodes so total storage and write capacity grow with the number of nodes. It is usually combined with replication, not a replacement for it.

questions.prompt: What problem does consistent hashing specifically solve?

options.text: It makes range queries fast
It minimizes how many keys must move when a node joins or leaves (~K/N)
It guarantees perfectly even load with no extra mechanism
It encrypts keys before storing them

questions.explanation: Consistent hashing minimizes data movement when the node set changes — only ~K/N keys relocate. Even load still requires virtual nodes.

questions.prompt: What are virtual nodes (vnodes) for in consistent hashing?

options.text: To encrypt data
To balance load by placing each physical node at many points on the ring
To replace replication
To make range scans efficient

questions.explanation: A few physical nodes on a ring can split it unevenly. Placing each node at many ring positions (vnodes) smooths the distribution.

questions.prompt: Why does partitioning by a timestamp key often create a hotspot?

options.text: Timestamps cannot be hashed
All new writes share the newest timestamp, so they all hit the single newest partition
Timestamps are too large to store
It makes range queries impossible

questions.explanation: With a monotonic key like a timestamp, every new write lands on the newest partition while older partitions sit idle — a classic hotspot.

questions.prompt: One celebrity's shard receives 1000x the reads of any other. Does better hashing fix it?

options.text: Yes, hashing always balances load perfectly
No — this is a single hot key, not skewed distribution; you need caching or key splitting
Yes, if you add more virtual nodes
No, the data must be deleted

questions.explanation: Hashing balances many keys, not one red-hot key. Mitigate a hot key by caching it or splitting it across sub-keys.

questions.prompt: Why is 'hash(key) mod N' a poor way to assign keys to nodes?

options.text: It is too slow to compute
Changing N remaps almost every key at once, causing a massive reshuffle
It cannot handle string keys
It always overloads node 0

questions.explanation: With mod N, adding or removing a node changes N and remaps nearly all keys, causing huge data movement and cache churn. Consistent hashing avoids this.
